title: Grade 3 Social Studies — Regions, Landforms, and Bodies of Water
subject: Social Studies
description: Practice with questions on plains, plateau, mountains, geography.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: What is a region?
choices: a single point with no area
an area grouped by one or more shared features

questions.question: Which landform is broad and mostly level?
Which is a raised area with a broad flat top?
Which feature lies between higher hills or mountains?
What is a peninsula?
choices: a place where all rivers meet
land with water on all sides
a stream flowing into a larger river
land with water on most sides and a connection to more land

questions.question: What is an island?
What is a mountain range?
choices: a group of connected or nearby mountains

questions.question: Which is a tributary?
choices: a mountain that divides two valleys
a smaller stream that flows into a larger river
a band of sand at the ocean

questions.question: Which landform is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides?
What may form where sediment builds up at the mouth of a river?
Why might people draw a region around places with many farms?
choices: They all belong to the same family.
They share a type of land use.
They all have the same town name.
They always get the same rainfall each day.

questions.question: Which feature marks a possible natural boundary between two places?
What is a shoreline?
choices: the edge where land meets water
the deepest part of a lake
the top of a tall mountain

questions.question: Where would a river generally move faster, with other conditions equal?
Which map could help find the highest land in a region?
choices: a bus schedule with no map

questions.question: Which detail best distinguishes a plateau from a low plain?
choices: It has some rock in its soil.
It is elevated above much of the surrounding land.

questions.question: What groups the places in a coastal region?
choices: They all use the same library.
They are all at the same street address.

questions.question: What is one way a mountain range can affect travel?
choices: Every road across it must be straight and flat.
It makes every town the same distance away.
It removes the need for bridges.
Roads may follow a pass between peaks.

questions.question: Which example groups places by a human feature?
choices: forests with the same tree species
towns that share one public transit system

questions.question: A map shows a narrow strip of land between two larger areas, with water on both sides. What is that feature?
